sections.title: Overview
descriptions: Cameron J. Paul is the chief of the American Fork Police Department. He has worked for the department since September 2008 and has led it since September 2021, first as interim chief and then as permanent chief.

In the Ben Schneider (Reckless Ben) case, Chief Paul received an update about the March 11 warrant operation and later reviewed the department’s actions. In a later interview, summarized from a rough app transcript, he said he did not believe a stop-sign violation occurred during the March 8 stop, while maintaining that another basis for the stop existed.

sections.title: Employment
descriptions: Cameron J. Paul began working for the American Fork Police Department on September 15, 2008. He later became a lieutenant.

Following Chief Darren Falslev’s retirement, effective September 29, 2021, Paul became interim police chief while the city conducted a formal selection process. American Fork announced Paul’s selection as its permanent chief of police on March 17, 2022.
As of September 24, 2026, Paul has served as permanent police chief for approximately four years and six months. Including his interim service, he has led the department for almost five years.

contents.text_value: March 8, 2026: According to a rough app transcript of a later interview, Chief Cameron Paul said Richardson had misremembered the stop-sign statute and that he did not believe a stop-sign violation occurred. Paul said the department reviewed the statute with Richardson. He maintained that another basis for the stop existed, but deferred explaining that basis until he could consult his findings.

March 11, 2026: Adamson’s recorded communications identify Chief Paul as receiving an update about the warrant operation and the people in custody. Only Adamson’s side of the call is recorded; it does not establish that Paul ordered a particular arrest or use of force.
